messages.body_plain:
Before opening this google-group, I used codewake as a platform to ask questions about brms for several months.
The brms codewake page can be found at

https://www.codewake.com/p/brms

Since I wasn't particularly happy with the features codewake offered, I now recommend using only this google-group (or github)
for discussions and questions about brms.

messages.subject: Extracting individual parameter estimates from a hierarchical model
messages.subject_clean: Extracting individual parameter estimates from a hierarchical model
messages.body_plain:
Is there a simple way of obtaining the estimates for each member of the grouping variable for the random effects, e.g. for each id in this model:

fit <- brm(reaction ~ days + (days | id), data = sleepstudy,  family = gaussian)

The coef() function just returns point estimates; is this already implemented in the brms package, or do I have to extract the samples from fit$fit and then manually add the fixed effect parameters to each individual?
messages.body_snippet:

fit <- brm(reaction ~ days + (days | id), data = slee

messages.subject: Re: Extracting individual parameter estimates from a hierarchical model
messages.subject_clean: Extracting individual parameter estimates from a hierarchical model
messages.body_plain:
You mean to also obtain CIs for the coefficients? Unfortunately, coef can only return point estimates as you say. I suggest the following:

# use regular expressions to extract the desired parameters
ran <- as.matrix(fit, pars = "^r_id.*,days")
fix <- as.vector(as.matrix(fit, pars = "^b_days"))

comb <- ran + fix
colMeans(comb)  # matches results of coef
<do whatever you want with the samples>

messages.subject: beta regression using the brms package
messages.subject_clean: beta regression using the brms package
messages.body_plain:
I would like to use brms to model the substrate conversion rate (response) as a function of initial substrate level (lac_init), enzyme dose (dose), temperature (temp), time (time), and pH (finalpH).

The response is a fraction: (initial substrate level - final substrate level) / (intial substrate level) bounded in the interval ]0 ; 1[ . I assume that Beta regression would be suitable for such a problem.

I can model this using the betareg package getting good results

package �betareg� was built under R version 3.2.5
Call:
betareg(formula = response ~ (sqrt(dose) + time + finalpH + temp)^2 + lac_init, data = as.data.frame(in_train))

Standardized weighted residuals 2:
    Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max
-7.1395 -0.5896 -0.0256  0.5600  8.1095

Coefficients (mean model with logit link):
                     Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
(Intercept)        21.1354940  4.4914824   4.706 2.53e-06 ***
sqrt(dose)         -0.8011171  0.0894485  -8.956  < 2e-16 ***
time               -0.2734958  0.0370627  -7.379 1.59e-13 ***
finalpH            -4.7567368  1.0552170  -4.508 6.55e-06 ***
temp               -0.8340544  0.1265061  -6.593 4.31e-11 ***
lac_init           -1.0515355  0.1043750 -10.075  < 2e-16 ***
sqrt(dose):time     0.0022238  0.0001349  16.487  < 2e-16 ***
sqrt(dose):finalpH  0.1847247  0.0210916   8.758  < 2e-16 ***
sqrt(dose):temp     0.0051239  0.0005236   9.785  < 2e-16 ***
time:finalpH        0.0559777  0.0085047   6.582 4.64e-11 ***
time:temp           0.0015417  0.0002115   7.289 3.13e-13 ***
finalpH:temp        0.1817306  0.0291293   6.239 4.41e-10 ***

Phi coefficients (precision model with identity link):
      Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
(phi)   73.648      5.939    12.4   <2e-16 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Type of estimator: ML (maximum likelihood)
Log-likelihood: 772.2 on 13 Df
Pseudo R-squared: 0.9243
Number of iterations: 68 (BFGS) + 5 (Fisher scoring)

The model performs quite well:
      RMSE   Rsquared
0.04320536 0.96851647

I would like to do the same model using brms:

brms_model <- brm(response ~ (sqrt(dose) + time + finalpH + temp)^2 + lac_init,
                  data = as.data.frame(in_train),
                  family = Beta())

But get the following error(s):

SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'beta(logit) brms-model' NOW (CHAIN 1).
  [1] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"
  [2] "Exception thrown at line 39: beta_log: First shape parameter[194] is 0, but must be > 0!"
  [3] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
  [4] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."

Any ideas on what i should do? Is the approach correct? do I need to specify a prior on the shape parameter? - and how to do it?

Any help would be highly appreciated

/Jannik

PS. I can provide the data-set if needed

Jannik

messages.subject: Re: beta regression using the brms package
messages.subject_clean: beta regression using the brms package
messages.body_plain:
The sampler has problems finding adequate initial values possibly because the scale of your predictors is too large.

If you use inits = 0, it should work, but it will be slow presumably because there are some many interactions that there is some sort of multicollineraity going on.

messages.body_plain:
I'm testing a simple ARMA model against a gaussian process smooth.

fit.ARMA <-
  brm(bf(DV  ~ 1),
      autocor = cor_arma(formula = ~ 1, p = 1, q = 1),
      family = student(link = "identity"),
      prior = c(set_prior("student_t(3,0,5)", class = "b"),
                set_prior("student_t(3,0,5)", class = "Intercept"),
                set_prior("student_t(3,0,1)", class = "ma"),
                set_prior("student_t(3,0,1)", class = "ar")),

           s(DaysTime, k = 50, bs = "gp") +

data)

I understand that in the ARMA model, the formula I used specifies the order of the observations as a covariate which leads me to wonder if am I missing something simple about how to supply the newdata to the predict function.

messages.subject: Re: Forecasts for an ARMA only model
messages.subject_clean: Forecasts for an ARMA only model
messages.body_plain:
The problem with brms is that it is so general that specifying forecasts for explicit time-series models (I mean those specified via argument autocor) through newdata is not trivial to implement.
In order to ARMA forecasts to make sense, we have to know the response values at those future time points to be predicted. Of course we don't know them or otherwise we wouldn't need forecasts. The canonical solution is to use the predicted values of future responses to compute further future responses, but this is not possible to specify via newdata (as least I didn't figure out yet how to do it). As a result, unfortunately and a bit embarrassingly, forecasts for structures implemented via autocor are not yet possible (it is just not the main focus of brms).

There is an open issue targeting this problem (https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/147) and I hope to provide a solution sooner rather than later.

messages.subject: Multivariate log-normal responses and effect sizes
messages.subject_clean: Multivariate log-normal responses and effect sizes
messages.body_plain:
Hello dear brms users,

I am trying to fit a brm model with multiple (four) lognormal-distributed response variables, and I would like to solicit your advice on several points. The model I have fitted has the following form:

model1 <- brm(
    formula = cbind(log(resp1), log(resp2), log(resp3), log(resp4)) ~ 1 + predictor1,
    data = data, family = gaussian(),
    prior = prior,
    warmup = 1000, thin = 10, iter = 10000,
    chains = 2, cores = parallel::detectCores(),

    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95)
    )

Basically, my idea was to log-transform these variables in order to be able to fit a gaussian multivariate brm model but I know this is a debatable choice (and it makes the interpretation of the posterior distribution in the log scale much less easy). Would anyone have alternative approach to suggest ?

Additionally, I was wondering how the effect sizes computations detailed in Gelman & Pardoe (2006) or Marsman et al. (2017) would be directly applicable in my case (i.e., a multivariate case) ? Is it possible to compute an estimate of the effect of predictor1 on a multivariate 'mixture' of the four response variables and / or on each response variable independently ?

Do not hesitate to redirect me toward external ressources (books, articles, forum topics, etc).

Best,

Ladislas

Gelman & Pardoe (2006):  - http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/published/rsquared.pdf
Marsman et al. (2017) - http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/published/birdseye.pdf (https://osf.io/3e5vh/)

messages.subject: Re: Multivariate log-normal responses and effect sizes
messages.subject_clean: Multivariate log-normal responses and effect sizes
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ladislas,

unfortunately, brms is not yet very flexible when it comes to multivariate models, but I am working on a way more general implementation within brms.
One other package that is currently more flexible for multivariate models is MCMCglmm, but I am not sure if it satisfies your needs since it doesn't support the lognormal distribution either.

I don't see any obstacles to applying the mentioned effect sizes independently to each response. The only difference between multiple separate gaussian models and one multivarite gaussian model is the estimation of the residual correlation matrix. Since brms fits separate coefficients for each response, you should have everthing available to compute the effect sizes separately.
I am not sure how one would compute a single effect size across responses, but I am admittedly not an expert in this regard.

Best
Paul
